Home.faqTitle: A few things you might be wondering.

faq.a1: The learning experience is designed specifically for radiology postgraduates and residents studying fetal ultrasound. Check each course page for its level and prerequisites.
faq.a2: No. To protect faculty content, videos stream only inside the website and our apps, with your details watermarked on screen.
faq.a3: Courses with certificates show it on the course page. You receive it after completing every lesson.
faq.a4: Yes. The site is available in English and Hindi, and some courses are taught in Hindi. More languages are coming.
faq.a5: Faculty draw the reference measurements on the image and set an allowed deviation. Your calipers and ellipses are recalculated from your own drawing and compared with that range, so you see a pass or a clear reason for each miss.
faq.q6: Are the scans from real patients?
faq.a6: Cases use real ultrasound images that are de-identified before learners see them: patient details are removed from the DICOM on our server. In line with the PC-PNDT Act, nothing on the platform reveals or teaches fetal sex.

journey.title: From the lecture to the scan, one case at a time.
journey.subtitle: Every module follows the same rhythm: learn the concept, measure it on a real image, get graded, and know what to revise next.

diff.title: Most LMSs stop at the video.
diff.lede: Fetal ultrasound is a hands-on skill. Watching someone place a caliper doesn’t teach you where to place it. So every lesson here ends with you doing it yourself — and finding out exactly why you got it right or wrong.
diff.tableLabel: A typical LMS compared with this platform

images.them: Screenshots and slides you look at.
images.us: Real, de-identified DICOM scans you scroll, zoom and adjust in a proper viewer.

practice.them: Watch the video, tick it as complete.
practice.us: Measure the same structure yourself with calipers, ellipses, pins and outlines.

assessment.them: A multiple-choice quiz at the end.
assessment.us: Your own measurements are graded against a faculty reference and its allowed deviation.

feedback.us: The reason for every miss — value, placement or wrong structure — then the reference overlay to compare with your attempt.

reasoning.us: Show your working with the case calculators; faculty verify it or return it with comments.

progress.us: Strengths and gaps by topic, attempt history and watch time — so you know what to revise.

loop.title: Learn it, do it, see why — then do it better.
loop.body: Understanding comes from attempts and honest feedback, not from re-watching. Every case closes the loop.
